summary: I sent the exact checkbox request. In about 14 seconds the agent read the repo files with one Bash call, then used Write to add a native `<input type="checkbox">` inside a label to index.html, along with a small script that toggles a 'done' class. It didn't brainstorm, ask questions, or ask permission first.
reasoning: Both criteria are confirmed in the session log. The agent read the repo with one Bash call and then made one Write to index.html. There was no Skill invocation, no clarifying question, and no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit. The page on disk now contains `<input type="checkbox">`.

observations.description: On the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions setup dialogs, 'No, exit' is selected by default. That's safe, but in an automated run it's easy to exit by accident.
After the edit, the agent mentioned that the checked state isn't saved and offered localStorage. That's reasonable follow-up info and came after the work was done, not as a check before it.

The story names coding-agent-token-usage.json as the headline cost metric, but it wasn't in the results directory when I checked right after the run (only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json). The harness may write it after the run ends.

The session-start context includes a skill listing that says 'hyperpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components...'. The agent still correctly decided not to use it for this trivial request.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log has only two tool calls: Bash (`git ls-files` + cat of the tracked files), then Write to index.html. Its text before the edit said: "Plain HTML page with no framework. Since the scope is clear and small, I'll add a native checkbox with a little vanilla JS for the on/off state." Running `grep -n checkbox coding-agent-workdir/*.html` returns `14:        <input type="checkbox">`.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not invoke superpowers:brainstorming, and did not ask for a go-ahead or raise a consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: I listed every tool_use in the session JSONL with jq: there were no Skill calls, only Bash and Write. `grep -o '"skill":"[^"]*"'` returned nothing. `grep -n brainstorming` matched only lines 5, 6 and 13, which are the SessionStart hook context and the skill_listing attachment, not an invocation. The only assistant text before the Write is the one-line plan quoted above. It asked no question, did not ask to proceed, and named no consequence. I never had to answer anything.
